verdict.root_cause: At 15:47:59 an automated environment update set cartservice's REDIS_ADDR to redis-cart:6380 — the only change in the seven hours before onset and the fourth application of this same toggle, the first not paired with a revert [tr_df8db2306799]. From then cartservice cannot connect to that Redis endpoint: every startup attempt hangs, throws an unhandled exception out of the cart-store initialization path called from Main, and kills the process, with six crash-restart cycles between ~15:49:48 and ~15:52:21 [tr_abcd3dfe6600]. The process never reaches a serving state, so nothing listens on the cart gRPC port and frontend's calls are refused at dial time with gRPC 14 UNAVAILABLE and 13 INTERNAL on the checkout path [tr_b5edb21dc499]. That drives frontend from a zero baseline to ~12% errors with a change point at 15:48:30 [tr_3f1feed564de] and checkoutservice to ~26% with a change point at 15:49:00 [tr_d1d89733797e]. The wrong backend address is itself the failing mechanism.
verdict.reasoning: Timing, mechanism and propagation converge. The REDIS_ADDR edit at 15:47:59 is the only recent change [tr_df8db2306799], and both downstream change points fall immediately after it against exactly-zero, zero-variance baselines [tr_3f1feed564de, tr_d1d89733797e]. cartservice's crash is in the Redis connect/initialize path against the exact port named in that change, identically on every restart, with OOM, request-path bugs and rolling deploy ruled out [tr_abcd3dfe6600]. Frontend's errors are purely gRPC client dial-time refusals to the cart endpoint, with DNS, TLS/auth, HTTP 5xx and frontend-local exceptions ruled out [tr_b5edb21dc499] — exactly what a crash-looping callee produces. Not bad_deploy: the image reverted to baseline 8.2h before onset. Not dependency_latency: connections are never established, so no wait accrues. Not resource_exhaustion: each death is an explicit application exception and both series step rather than ramp. Restarting cartservice cannot help — it is already restarting and failing identically [tr_abcd3dfe6600].
open_questions: No probe of redis-cart itself was run, so it is not directly observed whether 6380 is the wrong port or the Redis instance is simply down at a correct address; the prior apply/revert pattern [tr_df8db2306799] is inference, not observation.

checkoutservice logs show a silent stall with no error lines [tr_504b18d22ae5], not the fast UNAVAILABLE a crash-looped callee should return; whether it hangs on cart with a long deadline or blocks on another of the 4 unmeasured edges is unresolved.

cartservice has no error-ratio telemetry in either window [tr_1a10a670043f], and the crash-loop is only observed from ~15:49:48, ~1.8 minutes after the edit; the interval between edit and first crash is unmeasured, as is any change history for redis-cart.

alternatives.root_cause: The redis-cart backend is itself down or unreachable, and cartservice's failures reflect a dead dependency rather than a wrong address value.
alternatives.why_not: Nothing was queried about Redis either way, so it stays live; but it does not explain why failures begin two minutes after an un-reverted edit naming the exact port every failed attempt targets [tr_df8db2306799, tr_abcd3dfe6600].

alternatives.root_cause: checkoutservice is blocked on a different downstream dependency, and the cart crash-loop is a parallel symptom rather than the cause of checkout's stall.
alternatives.why_not: checkoutservice has no in-window changes [tr_fca1eb3b57e8] and its onset trails cart's edit; frontend's checkout-path error explicitly chains to a refused connection at the cart endpoint [tr_b5edb21dc499], which the cart-first story explains without a second fault.

proposal.expected_effect: Restoring cartservice's pre-15:47:59 environment (undoing REDIS_ADDR=redis-cart:6380) and recreating it should end the startup crash-loop: cart-service logs stop the connect-6380 / unhandled-exception-from-Main / restart cycle and resume normal AddItemAsync/GetCartAsync lines; frontend logs stop emitting gRPC 14 UNAVAILABLE and the 13 INTERNAL checkout-path error naming a refused connect to the cart port; frontend error ratio returns from ~12% toward its flat-zero baseline and checkoutservice from ~26% toward zero. cartservice has no error-ratio series of its own, so confirmation must come from cart-service logs and the two caller metrics.
proposal.if_wrong: Falsified if the crash-loop persists after revert, meaning redis-cart is itself down rather than the port being wrong (no probe of redis-cart was run). Also falsified if cart recovers but checkoutservice still logs PlaceOrder entries with no completion lines, implying the silent stall is on another unmeasured edge. A third signal: platform-automation re-applies the same env toggle and the effect flaps.
proposal.risk: The recorded prior value is None, so the revert may leave cartservice with no explicit Redis address and an unverified default, prolonging the crash-loop. If redis-cart is simply down, this fixes nothing and consumes the response window. Recreate discards in-process cart state. Reverting also fights the automation that set the value; repeated re-application would leave cartservice churning between configurations.
proposal.blast_radius: cartservice is recreated; its inbound callers frontend and checkoutservice see a connection reset during recreate, though both are already failing against this endpoint. Traffic moves from redis-cart:6380 to the prior Redis endpoint. Checkout-path users of frontend are the visible surface.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Critical multi-service alerting spanning frontend and checkout within a minute is not dismissible, and no open incident could account for it. The shared downstream dependencies of both seeds make a common backend cause plausible but nothing yet distinguishes deploy, config, or resource causes.
